episodes.199182: A strong low was centered over the Gulf of Maine on the morning of the 7th creating a tight pressure gradient across southern New England. This led to strong wind gusts generally 45 to 65 mph.
episodes.201206: A secondary cold front allowed northwest winds to briefly become elevated across the lower James River on the evening of March 6.
episodes.201293: An active weather pattern with a broad trough over the western states brought a series of low pressure systems to the region and provided rain, mtn snow, thunderstorms, and strong winds throughout the week.
episodes.201313: Diurnally induced afternoon showers and thunderstorms triggered small landslides on the 5th and 7th of March over central Puerto Rico.
